content.intro: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. In this lesson, focus on pure enumerations; then compare it with backed enumerations. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use enumerations when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. For enumerations, begin with pure enumerations. Also distinguish backed enumerations; enum cases; enum methods and interfaces. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Enumerations
content_blocks.code:
<?php
final class Tax { public function amount(int $price): int { return intdiv($price, 10); } }
final class Checkout { public function __construct(private Tax $tax) {} public function total(int $price): int { return $price + $this->tax->amount($price); } }
echo (new Checkout(new Tax()))->total(100) . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
